title: Drayton Wiser Heat Gateway Driver Help
author: Neil Colvin

driver.text: This guide describes Neil Colvin's Crestron Home platform driver for a local Drayton Wiser heating hub. One gateway connects to the hub and exposes its discovered rooms as managed thermostat children. The gateway provides optional whole-house hot water and Away Mode controls.

This guide applies to driver version 1.3.13. It explains installation, gateway and room controls, schedule editing and the supported equipment. Package availability does not establish Crestron certification.

notes.text: Set up the heating system and its room schedules in Wiser before adding the driver. Keep a stable local address or resolvable hostname for the hub, and keep its authentication secret private.

Schedules are shared hub objects. Editing an assigned schedule may affect other rooms that use the same schedule. Review the impact shown on the Edit Schedule page before saving. Away Mode applies to the system; individual room and hot water settings can subsequently be overridden.

After a state-changing command, the driver reads the hub's current state before publishing the result. Allow an in-progress command to finish before pressing again. The application should show the observed device state, rather than treating a command request as confirmation.

requirements.text: A Crestron Home processor supporting this SDK V2 entity/platform driver. Development testing used MC4-R and CP4-R processors with Crestron Home 4.011.0322. Earlier firmware has not been validated; the SDK version in the manifest is not a processor firmware version.
A reachable local Drayton Wiser hub with its hub authentication secret and configured heating rooms.
Local network connectivity between processor and hub, and a working Crestron Home setup and end-user application.
The driver package contains its required client library code. Dealers do not install the NUnit runner, processor test packages or development tools to use the production driver.

installation.text: Obtain the installable .pkg release asset. GitHub source ZIP and TAR archives are source code, not installable driver packages. Import the package using your normal Crestron Home driver installation process.
Add the Wiser Heat Gateway platform driver in Crestron Home Setup or Configure Pro. Supply the Hub IP Address / Hostname and Hub Secret. Keep the secret out of shared screenshots and support logs.

Choose Celsius or Fahrenheit for displayed temperatures. Room and schedule targets support 5 to 30 C (41 to 86 F), in steps equivalent to 0.5 C (0.9 F). Boost Increase is always configured in Celsius: 1 to 5 C, equivalent to 1.8 to 9 F. Boost Duration Minutes supports 5 to 1440. The defaults are Celsius display, a 2 C boost increase, and 60 minutes.

Enable Whole House Hot Water Control only when the hub supports hot water and you want that control exposed. Enable Allow Away Mode if the optional global Away control is required. Both settings default to disabled.

Allow the gateway to discover Wiser rooms, then assign its managed thermostat children to the appropriate Crestron Home rooms. Verify each child's identity and current temperature before operating it.

For an update, import the new package, wait for it to become available in the driver catalogue, and update the installed gateway through the configuration application. Importing a package alone does not update an installed instance. This is a V2 entity driver; its update does not require a full processor reboot. Verify room identities, assignments and current state after the update.
The driver has no activation-key purchase step. Its source and use remain subject to the repository's MIT License with Commons Clause; see Licensing and Copyright Information.

experience.text: The following screenshots illustrate the driver interface. Shown room names, readings and schedule times are examples, not required configuration values.

The gateway tile is shown on the Home screen. Its options page presents Hot Water and Away Mode when those features are enabled. Each control shows its current state and the available action. An unavailable or in-progress action must not be treated as a successful device change.

Each managed thermostat tile appears in its assigned room. Open it to view current temperature, adjust the heating target, start or stop a boost, or open Schedule. This is a heat-only interface; cooling and automatic heating/cooling changeover are not offered. An Off heating target is shown as Off rather than a negative temperature. The Set to 5°C (41°F) button deliberately resumes heating at the minimum target; adjust the normal thermostat control afterwards if needed.

The Schedule page shows the assigned schedule and whether schedule control is enabled. Select Schedule opens the available schedule choices. Enable and Disable change schedule control, and Edit opens the current shared schedule for editing.

Choose a day, then adjust the displayed time and setpoint slots. Day and time selectors open choice dialogs. An existing Off slot stays Off when its time or other slots are edited. Set to 5°C (41°F) changes only that pending slot to a heating temperature, which can then be adjusted normally. Save Day writes the selected day. Save All applies that day's entries to all days of the selected shared schedule. Cancel returns without saving the current edits. The page shows the schedule's shared impact and validation errors.

Open Select Schedule to choose from the schedules configured on the hub. Scroll to see further choices. The marked entry is the currently assigned schedule; the names depend on your Wiser configuration.
Open Day in the editor to choose the day whose entries you want to inspect or edit. The marked entry identifies the current editor day.
Open a time slot in the editor to choose its time. Scroll through the half-hour choices; the marked entry identifies the current value. Follow the page validation guidance before saving the schedule.

limitations.text: Only local Drayton Wiser heating behavior implemented by this driver is covered. Other products with Wiser branding and unvalidated hub variants are not implicitly supported.
Hot water controls depend on the hub's capabilities. Room heating controls do not provide cooling.
Schedule edits affect a shared hub schedule, not a private copy belonging to one Crestron room.

Crestron Home may retain stale child metadata after a driver entity or UI shape change. Check version and configuration first; consult support before removing a child, since its assignments or references may need to be restored.

If the gateway is offline, check hub power, local network reachability, the configured address and the hub secret. Compare the Wiser app's state, then refresh or reconnect the gateway. Include the driver, hub and processor versions when contacting support, but do not send credentials.

features.text: Local hub connection and discovery of managed room thermostat devices.
Current and target temperatures, Celsius/Fahrenheit display, heat-only thermostat control and room boost.
Schedule enablement, assignment, selection and shared day editing.
Heating and schedule feedback through room tile icons and status.
Optional whole-house Hot Water and global Away Mode controls on the gateway's Home tile.

environment.text: Read-only identification on 18 September 2026 recorded a Crestron CP4-R running Crestron Home 4.011.0322 and a Wiser CCTFR6313G2 hub, hardware generation 2, with firmware 4.36.33 (system version 4.36.33-9ad5712). The Google Android emulator runs Android 16 with Crestron Home app 4.6.18+pr (build 13148). These are observed development-environment versions, not a statement that the completed Crestron self-test has passed. Earlier development work also used an MC4-R with the same Crestron Home version.

models.text: The connected hub reports model CCTFR6313G2. Final submission validation is limited to that model unless additional models are independently tested. The driver manifest uses the display model Wiser Heat Gateway under manufacturer Drayton Wiser; that display name is not evidence of compatibility with every Wiser hub.

history.text: Accept thermostat endpoints reached through repeated Fahrenheit steps despite tiny floating-point rounding differences. The supported temperature limits and half-degree Celsius resolution are unchanged; genuinely out-of-range values remain rejected.

Keep rooms in Auto when changing their target temperature during a schedule refresh. If usable schedule information is unavailable, refuse the change without switching to Manual or cancelling an existing override.

Includes this illustrated help and dependency notices in the submission package. Retains the schedule selection, editor conflict protection, room readiness and command-result fixes from version 1.3.8, using WiserHeatAPIv2 1.1.2. Corrects Celsius/Fahrenheit display and command conversion, aligns adjustable ranges with the supported physical limits, and preserves Off settings until an explicit heating target is chosen.
Loads the driver definition independently of the submission assembly name. Routine unchanged room polling no longer repeats schedule diagnostics; actual schedule changes and failures remain visible.
